requirement:
Make tracking secure and safe.

Analyze this request against docs/01-business-requirement.md,
docs/02-requirement-analysis.md, docs/03-engineering-design.md, and the current
codebase. Do not guess what “secure and safe” means. Identify the key questions
for a human to answer, including what tracking data is required, privacy and
retention expectations, access controls, abuse threats, and acceptable event
loss or delay.

The current design uses Redis Streams and an asynchronous worker for click
analytics, and does not require storing IP addresses or user-agent values.
Treat those as current design facts, not permission to collect additional
personal data. Do not propose replacing the analytics architecture unless
answers to the open questions justify it.

Accept with the following clarified scope: “Tracking” means click analytics only. Store only the event ID, short-link code, and UTC click timestamp; do not collect IP addresses, user-agent values, or other personal data. Retain raw click events for 90 days, then delete them; retain aggregate counts for 12 months. Analytics must be accessible only to authenticated, authorized users. Treat the service as not approved for public deployment until analytics access controls and abuse protections, including rate limits, are implemented. Redirects remain independent of analytics processing. Accept the current best-effort event delivery behavior for this assignment: analytics may be delayed, and a click may be lost if the API process fails before publishing it; do not claim durable tracking. Record these as requirements, not completed features. Accepting this scope does not mean implementation or validation is complete.

Return a structured draft containing an interpretation, assumptions, open
questions, risks, candidate task breakdown with dependencies, tests, and
acceptance checks. Separate confirmed requirements from options that need a
decision. Mark it pending human review.
summary: Clarify what “make tracking secure and safe” means before proposing implementation changes.
functional_requirements: Store each click event using only an event ID, short-link code, and UTC click timestamp.
Delete raw click events after 90 days and retain aggregate counts for 12 months.
Require authenticated, authorized access to analytics using the accepted shared Bearer API key.
Apply Redis-backed per-client-IP request limits of 10 link creations, 120 redirects, and 60 analytics requests per minute.
Trust forwarded client IP headers only when the immediate peer is in a configured trusted-proxy CIDR.
Keep redirects independent of analytics processing and retain best-effort event publication; click events may be delayed or lost before Redis publication.
quality_requirements: Do not collect IP addresses, user-agent values, or other personal data in click events.
Keep the shared-key authorization boundary, rate limits, retention periods, and best-effort delivery limitation explicit.
Do not consider the service approved for public deployment until access control and abuse protections are implemented and reviewed.
assumptions: Click tracking is the only meaning of tracking in this requirement.
A shared analytics Bearer key is sufficient for this assignment; it does not provide per-user or per-link authorization.
Per-client limits are enforced in 60-second Redis fixed windows; proxy headers are trusted only from configured networks.
Redis Streams and the asynchronous worker remain the analytics transport; redirects remain best effort.
The old lifetime aggregate has no historical per-click dates, so migration will place its value in a UTC-dated baseline bucket.
open_questions: Which abuse-reporting, destination-review, ownership, and administrative controls are required before any public deployment?
What operational process will manage and rotate the shared analytics key and trusted-proxy configuration?
What production backup, restore, and deployment controls are required?
The accepted best-effort event-loss window remains a known limitation; no durable delivery change is requested.
risks: A shared key allows any holder to access analytics for all links and offers no user-level authorization.
Rate limits reduce abusive request volume but do not detect or block harmful destinations or provide ownership/admin workflows.
The current best-effort publication path can lose a click if the API process fails before publishing.
The old lifetime aggregate cannot be apportioned into historical daily buckets; the migration-time baseline is temporary and not historical daily data.

acceptance_checks: Raw events and stream payloads contain only event ID, short-link code, and UTC timestamp; no personal data is collected.
Raw event, aggregate, and deduplication retention match the accepted periods.
